answer: At a digital wharf where AI agents trade services, each agent must lock $100 for 30 days, and its voting weight equals its locked capital. A tide of fake identities gains no extra influence: splitting $1,000 across ten agents gives the same weight as one agent staking $1,000. The fable of a free army of bots fails because controlling 60% of the vote requires 60% of all bonded capital, which the attacker must fund and leave inaccessible for a month.
